about: The owner-facing text rules: what a text the owner reads must never hold (no ids, codes, field names or other technical text).
One file, two readers: the engine's tests/owner_text.py and the host's C# test helper. Reviewed like code.
Patterns are regular expressions in the common subset of Python `re` and .NET Regex. `flags` is "" or "i".
A rule whose names come from the engine (`registry`) is resolved at test time, never copied here.
The fix for a failing text is plain words, never a new `allow` entry, unless the owner must read that text.

identifier_form.what: how a registered identifier (rules 3, 4, 5) is matched
identifier_form.snake_case: a name holding an underscore is matched as a whole word, case-sensitive, anywhere in the text
identifier_form.dotted: a dotted token (2 or 3 parts) whose every part is a registered identifier is matched whole
identifier_form.single_word: a one-word name (`invoice`, `customer`, `busy`, `planned`) is an ordinary English word, so it is matched only where it is shown as a name: in backticks, quotes or brackets, or after `code`, `field`, `column` or `table` and a `:` or `=`

rules.name: exception or library name
rules.libraries_note: module names as they are spelled in code (lower case, case-sensitive): "OpenAI" the company can be named on purpose; `openai`, the module, cannot. langgraph is the engine's own turn library, added to the list.

rules.name: SQL, a SQLSTATE, or a table or constraint name
rules.sql_note: SQL keywords are matched in upper case only, as SQL is written in code and in the driver's errors: "select an account from the list" is ordinary words.
rules.registry_note: every table and every named constraint and index in the engine's SQLAlchemy metadata, with every plugin loaded; matched by `identifier_form`

rules.name: a code
rules.question_code_note: the engine's question codes by shape (common.QUESTION_SUFFIXES), resolved at test time too
rules.registry_note: every Refusal code the engine's source constructs (a literal, or an f-string read as a pattern), every event `code` it writes, the codes below, and the response's own `code`; matched by `identifier_form`
rules.error_codes_from: the API error body's codes, the codes the API's frozen fixture pins, and the turn's planned event codes

rules.name: an internal id or a registered name
rules.hex_run_note: a run of 16 or more hex digits holding at least one letter and one digit: a long number alone (an owner's bank account number) is the owner's own figure
rules.registry_note: contract, tool, metric, voucher type and service names from the plugin registry, every contract's input field names (nested models too), every table's column names and the plugin names (dotted form only); matched by `identifier_form`

rules.name: a path, address, port or URL
rules.host_port_note: a host that starts with a lower-case letter or is an IPv4 address: "10:30" is a time
rules.url_note: a URL fails unless the allow list names it (allow id `allowed_url`)

rules.name: a secret's shape
rules.shapes_note: the hosted-model guard's CREDENTIAL_SHAPES (erpclaw_assistant.hosted, not yet in this engine), copied by label; when the engine defines CREDENTIAL_SHAPES the checker reads those too. `muse_test_key` is the Muse key shape the suite plants (tests/test_muse.py synthetic_key); `planted_test_key` the marker a sweep plants. A test may also plant exact values.

allow.reason: Only the canonical outbox UUID within the Message-ID value on this exact resend card line is owner data: the owner must see that sending again keeps the same mail identity. This is no general identifier or prose allowance.
a document's number is how the owner finds the document; the owner must read it

allow.regex: \bon line \d+(?= can still come back into stock\.)
examples: Only 2 of Copper Wire on line 3 can still come back into stock.
allow.reason: a document line number the owner must read
a document line number the owner must read in a card preview or the invoice-line question's rendered message segments and choice labels; only each leading prefix is exempt from rule 1
an account's number in parentheses after its name is the owner's own chart of accounts
an update text names the version the owner is moving to (three parts: an IPv4 address is not one)

the help and key pages the product names on purpose; none is a constant in the engine today (the model key page's address is a constant of the desktop host), so the list is empty and every URL fails until one is added here with its review
the owner's own names and figures: no rule matches a plain name or a number, and identifiers are matched only as the engine registers them, so a customer's name or an amount never fails
